## United Nation's Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)



:::: columns

::: {.column width="55%"}

The SDGs constitute a framework for addressing the world's most pressing challenges. They provide a shared language and set of objectives for governments, organizations, and researchers to align their efforts toward a sustainable future [@un_2030_agenda_2015].

<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false title="Definition of sustainable development"}
As the departure point serves the **Brundtland report** issued by @wced_our_common_future_1987:

> *Sustainable development is development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.*
:::

:::

::: {.column width="5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="35%"}

![Brundtland report issued in 1987](./images/brundtland_report_book_cover.jpg){width=80%}

:::


::::


## From SDGs to quantifiable indicators

:::: columns

::: {.column width="5%"}

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}


Sustainability becomes operational via indicators that bridge between SDG goals and tangible outcomes. **Indicators can be measured, predicted and optimized for.**


**Example: Indicator 7.2.1**

- **2015:** 15.6%
- **2023:** 18.0%

::: {style="font-size: 0.8em;"}

**Sources** : 

* UN SDG Report 2026 [@un_sdg_report_2026_goal7]
* UN metadata for indicator 7.2.1 [@un_sdg_metadata_721].

:::

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-card}
::: {.sdg-taxonomy-flow}

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-step}
**Goal 7**  Affordable and Clean Energy
:::

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-arrow}
↓
:::

:::

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-arrow}
↓
:::

:::

## Computational Science and Engineering (CS\&E)

::: {.framework-card .cse-overlap-card}

<div class="framework-center-line">
  ... sits at the intersection of applied mathematics, computer science and applications in engineering and science.</div>

<div style="height: 0.1em;"></div>

:::: columns

::: {.column width="60%"}

**Motivation:** Model-based design or ~ decision-support in complex systems of physics-based or mechanistic core. 

**Objective:** Uncertainty-aware and error-controlled prediction, introspection or reanalyis of coupled processes.

**Focus:** Methods, algorithms, implementation, and software along with their effective deployment.

**Challenges:** Given by multi-physics and multi-scale coupling, complex geometries, boundary conditions, the necessity for high-throughput tasks and data-rich workflows.

:::
 
::: {.column width="40%"}

<div style="height: 0.5em;"></div>

![](./images/cse-overview.png)

:::

::::
:::

## Sustainability and CS\&E 

**Observation**: CS\&E often contributes indirectly, but rarely names sustainability explicitly:

```{=html}
<div class="framework-bridge">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Application-facing view</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>sustainability is a societal objective</li>
      <li>SDGs are visible in application-facing projects</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-bridge-arrow" aria-hidden="true">↔</div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Method-oriented view</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>CS&amp;E is an enabling technology</li>
      <li>sustainability is rarely explicit in method-oriented CS&amp;E research</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

CS\&E publications focus on accuracy, runtime, scalability, and robustness, yet rarely frame methodological design as sustainability choices. That mismatch motivates a second question.

>
> If CS&amp;E helps design a more sustainable world, how sustainable is CS&amp;E itself?
>

## A simple framing for sustainable CS\&E

::: columns

::: {.column width="32%"}

**Sustainable computing**

- resource-aware models
- efficient algorithms
- energy-aware workflows

:::

::: {.column width="32%"}

**Sustainable software**

- reusable code
- reproducible results
- maintainable ecosystems

:::

::: {.column width="36%"}

**Stakeholder action**

- incentives
- infrastructure
- education

:::

::::

Sustainable CS\&E emerges when these three dimensions reinforce each other.


## Three sustainability aspects, and why they matter now

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">

    <ol>
      <li>Energy footprint of computational work</li>

    </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">

      <li>workflows are becoming more complex</li>
      <li>software stacks are becoming more fragile</li>
      <li>AI-HPC pipelines increase both opportunity and waste</li>
      <li>scientific value is easily lost in irreproducible computation</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## The idea of sustainability based on Carlowitz

We typically attribute the sustainability idea to **Hans Carl von Carlowitz**.

- early forestry formulation in *Sylvicultura oeconomica*  [@carlowitz_1713_biblio]

- manage forests such that harvest does not outrun regrowth
- it turned forest use into an explicit long-term management problem
- ideas existed before Carlowitz, but he made them operational and widely known

::: {style="font-size: 0.7em;"}
> "..."
> Daß es eine continuirliche, beständige und *nachhaltende Nutzung* gebe, weil es eine unentbehrliche Sache ist, ohne welche das Land in seinem Esse nicht bleiben mag.
> --- *Hans Carl von Carlowitz, Sylvicultura oeconomica* [@carlowitz_1713_biblio]
:::


## Carlowitz' motivation was economic pressure 

::: columns

::: {.column width="34%"}

Carlowitz was a mining administrator in Saxony facing a **decision-support problem**:

- reconstruction after war
- expanding mining and metallurgy
- rising timber prices and transport distance
- growing pressure on economically accessible wood

**His core question**: 


:::

```{=html}
    loading="lazy"></iframe>
```

:::

:::::

How do we keep a resource-dependent system running when demand grows faster than renewal?



## It's a time-scale challenge

Key challenge: The scope of the decision rested on a time-scale much shorter than the regeneration time of the system it controlled. *Sustainable forest management* requires predictive decision support whenever resource response times exceed operational decision horizons


```{=html}

    data-external="1"
    src="wood_response_times_matrix.html"
    width="100%"
    height="610"
    style="display:block; border:none; background:#f4f7fb; border-radius:12px;"
    loading="lazy"></iframe>
```


## From Carlowitz to the Sustainable Development Goals

:::: columns

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-card}

**Carlowitz**: 

One renewable resource, one stock, one regeneration process
$$S_{t+1}=S_t+G_t-H_t$$

:::

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.sdg-taxonomy-card}

**SDGs today**: 

Many interacting resources, many coupled indicators, many delayed responses

17 Goals &nbsp;•&nbsp; 169 Targets &nbsp;•&nbsp; &gt;230 Indicators
  
:::


::: 
::::

```{=html}
<div class="framework-center-line">

A common principle: </br>
When regeneration is slower than decision cycles, today's decisions determine tomorrow's possibilities. Sustainability is not mainly about indicators. It is about governing delayed dynamics:

\[T_{\mathrm{system}} > T_{\mathrm{decision}}\]
</div>

```

## Let's model and formalize

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>State and dynamics</h3>
    <p><strong>Resource</strong> <code>R(t)</code></p>
    <p><strong>Dynamics</strong></p>
    <p>\[
    \frac{dR}{dt}=G(R)-D(R)+E
    \]</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>G</strong>: regeneration</li>
      <li><strong>D</strong>: depletion</li>
      <li><strong>E</strong>: managed intervention</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Governance and viability</h3>
    <p><strong>Decision</strong> <code>u(t)</code></p>
    <p><strong>Implementation</strong></p>
    <p>\[
    \tau_I \frac{dI}{dt}=c\,u-I
    \]</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>c</strong>: compliance</li>
      <li><strong>I</strong>: realized impact</li>
      <li><strong>R(t)\in \mathcal{K}</strong>: viable region</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">Sustainability means keeping a regenerating system inside a viable region despite delay, depletion, and imperfect implementation.</div>
```


## What changes from one domain to the next?

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>The structure stays the same</h3>
    <ol>
      <li>resource</li>
      <li>regeneration</li>
      <li>depletion</li>
      <li>governance</li>
      <li>compliance</li>
      <li>viability</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Only the interpretation changes</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>forest: timber stock</li>
      <li>software: usability</li>
      <li>methods: methodological capability</li>
      <li>computing: effective compute</li>
      <li>humans: scientific capability</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## The internal perspective

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>If CS&amp;E wants to be credible</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>it must reflect on its own energy footprint</li>
      <li>it must preserve its software and knowledge</li>
      <li>it must sustain its future methodological relevance</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>The three sustainability dimensions</h3>
    <ol>
      <li>sustainable computing</li>
      <li>sustainable software and methods</li>
      <li>sustainable human capability</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">If CS&amp;E helps design a more sustainable world, it must also sustain its own computational ecosystems.</div>
```


## CS\&E bottlenecks are shifting

::: columns

::: {.column width="48%"}

**Traditional bottlenecks**

- compute access
- parallelization competence
- memory and storage
- raw implementation effort

:::

::: {.column width="52%"}

**Emerging bottlenecks**

- workflow complexity
- software fragility
- reproducibility gaps
- AI integration
- long-term maintainability

:::

::::


## Sustainable computing is about deliberate trade-offs

It asks how computational work should be designed so that scientific benefit, runtime, and resource use are balanced consciously.


## Available compute is a finite regenerative resource

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Resource</h3>
    <p><strong>Available compute</strong> <code>C(t)</code></p>
    <p>Includes hardware, energy, queue time, cloud access, budget, and carbon budget.</p>
    <p>\[
    \dot C = G_C - L_C
    \]</p>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Interpretation</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>G<sub>C</sub></strong>: hardware, energy efficiency, funding, algorithms</li>
      <li><strong>L<sub>C</sub></strong>: larger simulations, UQ, optimization, digital twins</li>
      <li>finite computational opportunity must be allocated deliberately</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">The key question is not how to minimize compute at all costs, but how to turn finite compute into the most trustworthy insight.</div>
```

## Green computing versus sustainable computing

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Green computing asks</h3>
    <p>How can we reduce computational energy consumption?</p>
    <p style="margin-top:1rem;">Important, but incomplete.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Sustainable computing asks</h3>
    <p>\[
    K=\eta(M)\,C
    \]</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>K</strong>: generated knowledge</li>
      <li><strong>M</strong>: methodological capability</li>
      <li><strong>\eta = K/C</strong>: knowledge return per computational investment</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">The goal is not minimal compute. The goal is maximal trustworthy information return per computational investment.</div>
```


## Sustainable computing means allocating effort where it matters

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Three levers</h3>
    <ol>
      <li>Hardware efficiency</li>
      <li>Algorithmic efficiency</li>
      <li>Model efficiency</li>
    </ol>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>What that means in practice</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>invest degrees of freedom only where they matter</li>
      <li>connect accuracy targets to computational effort</li>
      <li>let quantities of interest drive computational investment</li>
      <li>spend extra effort only where it changes the answer materially</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">Adaptive methods increase effective compute because they increase the value extracted from each computational unit.</div>
```


## Regeneration and depletion in computational ecosystems

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Regeneration</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>more efficient hardware</li>
      <li>improved energy infrastructure</li>
      <li>better scheduling</li>
      <li>adaptive numerical methods</li>
      <li>improved software</li>
      <li>AI-assisted workflows</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Depletion</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>larger simulations</li>
      <li>increasing model fidelity</li>
      <li>uncertainty quantification</li>
      <li>optimization and control</li>
      <li>digital twins</li>
      <li>more ambitious scientific questions</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```


## Monitoring resource consumption

- measurement creates visibility
- visibility enables accountability
- accountability can shape better workflows


## Why ALUMET matters

- application-level energy attribution is hard on shared CPU/GPU systems
- runtime alone is often an unreliable proxy for energy consumption
- sustainable CS\&E needs measurement that reflects actual computational cost
- ALUMET helps close the gap between raw telemetry and actionable energy awareness


## ALUMET as enabler

- modular, lightweight framework for energy and system measurement
- plugin-based pipeline: gather, transform, export
- adaptable across heterogeneous hardware and workflow contexts
- enables downstream analysis and interpretation through tools such as Alumet-Insight
- turns energy awareness into something usable for research software and workflows


## Software is the heart of CS\&E

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Scientific role</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>software carries methods into practice</li>
      <li>software preserves or loses knowledge</li>
      <li>software quality shapes long-term scientific impact</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>The key shift</h3>
    <p>The sustained resource is not the artifact itself.</p>
    <p><strong>It is software usability inside an evolving ecosystem.</strong></p>
  </div>
</div>
```


## Sustainable software as a viability problem

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Resource dynamics</h3>
    <p><strong>Usability</strong> <code>U(t)</code></p>
    <p>\[
    \dot U = -\delta U + \eta m
    \]</p>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>\delta</strong>: ecosystem drift</li>
      <li><strong>m</strong>: realized maintenance</li>
      <li><strong>\eta</strong>: maintenance effectiveness</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Viability</h3>
    <p>\[
    U(t)\ge U_{\min}
    \]</p>
    <p>Software remains viable only if maintenance keeps pace with drift.</p>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">Software sustainability is an ecosystem problem: usability decays unless maintenance continuously regenerates it.</div>
```


## Planning versus implementation

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Planned maintenance</h3>
    <p><strong>Decision</strong> <code>I(t)</code></p>
    <p>What a group lead, PI, or project team intends to invest.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Realized maintenance</h3>
    <p>\[
    m(t)=c(t)\,I(t)
    \]</p>
    <p><strong>Compliance</strong> determines how much planned work becomes actual upkeep.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```


## Sustainable software means more than code availability

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Properties of sustainable software</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>maintainability</li>
      <li>reproducibility</li>
      <li>accessibility</li>
      <li>extensibility</li>
      <li>portability</li>
      <li>community uptake</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Two failure modes</h3>
    <ul>
      <li><strong>resource failure</strong>: too little maintenance planned</li>
      <li><strong>governance failure</strong>: maintenance planned, but not implemented</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```


## Sustainability emerges from feedback loops

- usability increases adoption
- adoption increases maintenance willingness
- maintenance preserves usability
- declining usability can trigger the opposite loop


## Sustainable methods as a race between questions and methods

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Two evolving quantities</h3>
    <p><strong>Required decision capability</strong> <code>Q(t)</code></p>
    <p><strong>Available methodological capability</strong> <code>M(t)</code></p>
    <p>\[
    \Gamma(t)=Q(t)-M(t), \qquad \Gamma \le 0 \text{ for viability}
    \]</p>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Interpretation</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>demand drives innovation</li>
      <li>success creates new demand</li>
      <li>adaptivity slows obsolescence</li>
      <li>continuous innovation is required just to keep pace</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">Computational science is a race between expanding questions and the community's ability to answer them.</div>
```


## Methodological success creates future demand

- more methods enable more ambitious questions
- more ambitious questions raise required decision capability
- adaptivity slows methodological obsolescence
- continuous innovation is required merely to keep pace


## Sustainable human capability

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>The regenerative layer beneath CS&amp;E</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>education</li>
      <li>mentoring</li>
      <li>scientific collaboration</li>

</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">Human capability is the deepest regenerative resource in CS&amp;E because it renews every other layer of the ecosystem.</div>
```

```text

        ↓

```

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
```

## My stronger claim today

The manuscript was necessary.

Sustainable CS\&E is not merely a topic area. It is a methodology.


## The core methodological question

Sustainable CS\&E asks:

How do we maximize trustworthy information return per computational investment?


## Computational investment and information return

```{=html}
<div class="framework-two-col">
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Computational investment includes</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>compute time</li>
      <li>energy</li>
      <li>human development effort</li>
      <li>workflow complexity</li>
      <li>software maintenance</li>
      <li>data generation and curation</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
  <div class="framework-card">
    <h3>Information return includes</h3>
    <ul>
      <li>reduced uncertainty</li>
      <li>trustworthy predictions</li>
      <li>actionable design guidance</li>
      <li>transferable method knowledge</li>
      <li>reusable software and workflows</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="framework-center-line">The methodological task is to increase trustworthy information return per unit of computational investment.</div>
```


## This is already native to CS\&E

- error control already asks what accuracy is needed
- adaptivity already allocates resources selectively
- model hierarchies already trade cost against insight
- numerical analysis already disciplines approximation


## Sustainable CS\&E is principled approximation

The point is not to compute less at all costs.

The point is to compute as much as needed, for the right reason, at the right fidelity.


## AI makes this more urgent

- AI can amplify scientific productivity
- AI can also amplify waste, opacity, and fragility
- CS\&E has the tools to make AI workflows more principled


## My synthesis

Sustainable CS\&E is the disciplined pursuit of lasting scientific value from computational effort.


## Final message

If CS\&E wants to remain a key enabling discipline, it must make sustainability explicit in how it designs methods, software, and workflows.
